text: This diver is 45 feet down off Cape Cod when a humpback whale scoops him up, and everything goes black.
It really happened, in 2021, to a lobster diver named Michael Packard.
Old stories say a man can live for days inside a whale's belly.
Bad news: a humpback's mouth can open around 10 feet.
Good news: its throat is only about the size of your fist, so he can't go down.
But he's stuck in the dark, in its closed mouth, for 30 to 40 seconds.
Then the whale rises to the surface, shakes its head, and spits him out.
He walked out of the hospital that same day, bruised all over, with no broken bones.
But one whale's throat is big enough to swallow you: the sperm whale. It can gulp a giant squid whole.
